_why: THE RATCHET, keyed by scan scope. 71 warnings printed on every push for weeks and blocked nothing — detected, never prevented. Each rule now carries a reviewed count and a reason PER SCAN SCOPE, because the pre-push hook never scans the whole repo: it scans the root with exclusions, then each touched project. Exceeding a scope's budget FAILS the push; dropping below it rewrites that budget down. The number can only go down. A rule firing with no entry fails, so a new class of problem cannot arrive quietly. Ships with NO scopes: each auto-baselines on its first scan of your own tree, so the ratchet starts from your code rather than from someone else's reviewed counts.
